lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.23 - A Listen, point and say

details: Listen, Point and Say checks understanding of word meaning and sound. Listen and point shows they match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for focused listening, accurate pointing to the correct food items, and clear pronunciation of the container phrases.
“I'm so excited because I'm planning a big picnic for us all! My shopping list is quite long, with lots of things in tins, bags, and bottles. Can you help me find everything we need to buy?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.23 - B. Listen and circle

details: Listen and Circle continues checking sound–image connections. Students practise listening for specific information and clearly circling an image based on what they hear.
Look for careful listening, accurate choices, clear circling, and neat work in students’ books.

“Thank you for finding everything! Now, my friend has sent me a voice message with the final shopping list. The supermarket is quite noisy, so I need your expert ears to help me listen carefully and circle the exact items we need to put in our trolley.”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.81 - A Look & write

details: Look and write consolidates the use of container phrases. Students select the correct singular or plural container from the word bank to accurately describe the items in the pictures.
Look for accurately completed phrases that correctly use the singular or plural container to match each picture.
“Now that we're back from the supermarket, let's organise our food for the picnic. Can you help me write the correct labels for all of these different items?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.81 - B Look & write

details: Look and write provides controlled practice of forming sentences with 'I need...'. Students must look at the picture, count the items, and write complete sentences using the correct number and container phrase.
Look for accurately written sentences that include the correct number, plural container, and food item for each of the five thoughts.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.24 - C. Ask and Answer

details: Ask and answer provides controlled speaking practice of the target question ‘How many... do you need?’ Students use the picture prompts to ask and answer about quantities, reinforcing the new grammar.
Look for accurate use of the question structure with the correct container phrase, and listen for clear, logical answers from partners.

“We have a lot of things in our trolley for the picnic, but I've lost track of the quantities. There’s a lot to remember! Let's do a final check. Can you ask your partner how many of each item we have?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.24 - D. Complete your shopping list. Then ask and answer to complete your friend's list. 10m]

details: This activity provides personalised and communicative practice. Students first complete their own shopping list, then interview a partner to get real information and complete a second list, creating an information gap.
Look for confident and natural conversation between pairs using the target question, and accurately completed shopping lists that reflect the information their partner provided.

“Okay, planners, it's time to create your own perfect picnic list! First, decide how much you want of each item. Then, interview your friend to find out what they want for their picnic, because we need to make sure we buy enough for everyone!”

The Chant consolidates the target question form (How many... do you need?) and container phrases through rhythm and repetition. It allows students to practise natural intonation and sentence stress in a fun, high-energy closer.
Look for enthusiastic participation, clear pronunciation of the questions and quantities, and a correct sense of rhythm and intonation from the whole class.
“That was excellent work creating your shopping lists! Now that all our planning for the picnic is done, let's finish with a fun chant to practise asking for all the groceries we need.”

Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
